messages:
emily: Heads-up — received a support ticket where Org B could see Org A's Quick Preview content when rapidly switching workspaces. Customer pasted a screenshot, they saw a draft from a different org. :eyes:
raj: I just tried a rapid org switch in staging and can repro 60% of the time. Quick steps: switch org -> open runlist -> hover preview -> preview shows other org's content. Looks like a cache key problem on the prefetch path.
marta: That smells like the change we merged last week that moved preview prefetch to the edge cache (PR #4321). We removed some headers from the cache key to reduce churn.
emily: Copy of the curl I used to repro:
```
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'x-org-id: org-b' 'https://console.staging.internal/_/preview?run=abc123'
```
Response included run metadata from org-a.
raj: On the proxy logs I see the request forwarded without x-org-id in the internal call to /prefetch because we use session cookie to route, but the cache decorator constructs key from path + accept-language only. Example key: `quickpreview:/run/abc123:en-US` which obviously misses tenant.
alex: I can push a hotfix to include tenant in cache key (session or x-org-id) and add defensive check in the preview handler that asserts run.org_id === request.org_id before returning cached payload.
marta: +1 for the defensive check. I'd prefer we scope cache keys to an explicit tenant field rather than rely on cookies. Cookie races are the root cause here — fast switches can update cookie mid-request.
emily: Agree. Two action items: 1) short-term revert the edge prefetch heuristic change (makes key tenant-less) or add tenant to key; 2) add a runtime assertion to guard returned previews. Which do we ship to canary?
raj: Ship assertion first (low risk) and enable telemetry when it fires (count + sample payload). If we get hits we can block and fail closed. Then ship cache-key fix.
alex: I'll make a small PR:
- inject `X-Prefetch-Tenant` into internal calls
- cache key = `${tenant}:${path}:${acceptLang}`
- add server-side assertion: if cached.org_id != req.tenant -> log+discard cache and increment metric
I'll add unit tests.
marta: Do we want an emergency rollout plan? This touches routing + cache; prod traffic is sensitive.
emily: Yes. Plan: deploy assertion change to 10% of console traffic canary, watch metric `preview.cache_tenant_mismatch`. If under thresholds after 30m promote and roll cache-key change at 5% -> 50% -> 100%.
raj: Also flag any customer-facing incidents: create ticket, add temporary mitigation for impacted customer (manual purge of preview cache for their org), and include mitigation in status page if needed.
alex: Deploy-bot started a canary for the assertion PR on staging (canary id ci-17555). Will open PR link in thread.
deploy-bot: canary deploy ci-17555 started: service=console-prefetch, route=canary-10%, commit=ae3f7d (assertion+telemetry).
emily: Good. Also add an E2E test that runs rapid org-switch scenarios in the harness (simulates cookie swap mid-flight). That should prevent regressions.
marta: I'll own the rollout checklist + postmortem if this surfaces in prod.
raj: For telemetry, include sampled payload (scrub PII) and the raw run.id + expected org to help repro.
emily: Thanks all. I'll file a short incident record, add the support ticket link, and follow up once the canary runs. :lock: :bug:
